Purpose: Measured per-stage cost rates of the Palace response worker / reducer / ordinary local-edge stages on one r8g.48xlarge node (192 ranks, frozen executable 170439c4a9fc5d5ce329310812055be5fb83a4a7f288024b57b3b83551cbe70b, streaming one-pass Gram reducer at block size 48) refit by refit_cost_model.py from the 6-coupon device library qualification library-qualification.json (tool commit 7c7bb5fe5, PBS 47080, 47081, 47082, 47083, 47084, 47086, 47105, 47106, 47107, 47108, 47109, 47110, 47207, 47212, 47213, 47214, 47215, 47216, 47218, 47219, 47250, 47256, 47289, 47290, 47291, 47298, 47300, 47301, 47335, 47336, 47348, 47349, 47356, 47358, 47467). Every rate is on the reference mesh spatial-3-edge-5d3b5e644745 and is the LARGEST the run's coupons imply once scaled to it by the exact H1 ratio (fail-closed: the 1x estimate is at least the measured wall of every stage of every coupon; SelfCheck). estimate_stages.py scales them to another hybrid prism-tube coupon mesh by the exact H1 DOF ratio with 1x / 1.5x / 2x the measured mean PCG counts.

MeasuredMesh.Label: spatial-3-edge-5d3b5e644745 identity (device library 2026-09-22; 2,635,846 tets + 373,347 prisms + 28,719 pyramids, 714,404 nodes)

ReducerEvaluationFractionRule: the fraction of the measured ReducerPairSeconds that is the per-source-evaluation work (archive read, gradient, face-neighbour exchange, quadrature-point evaluation of every source of a block pair: N x ceil(N / b) evaluations at block size b) - it shrinks with a larger PALACE_RESPONSE_BLOCK_SIZE (decision 62(1): default 6 -> 48); the remainder is the Gram work proportional to the source pairs N (N + 1) / 2, independent of b. Measured by the decision-62 step-1 acceptance (PBS 46685, two-edge-8dd4bc70f183 p4, 78 sources, H1 7.97M, frozen b28 executable, the same archive reduced at b = 6 and b = 48): Operator Construction 86.9 s at b = 6 (1,014 evaluations, 91 block pairs) vs 15.25 s at b = 48 (156 evaluations, 3 block pairs) -> 0.0835 s per evaluation, 2.2 s of pair-scaled Gram: evaluation fraction 0.975 at b = 6, recorded as 0.97 (the Gram remainder rounded up: fail-closed side) KEPT by the library-qualification.json refit: one block size (48) cannot separate the evaluation and Gram parts; ReducerPairSeconds is inverted through this split at the reference source count so the 1x reducer estimate covers every coupon of the run
ReducerResidentFieldGBRule: Palace peak memory the reducer adds per resident archived source field (V, E and their grid functions with ghosts), per million H1 DOFs of the stage: 2b fields are resident per block pair, so the reducer peak at block size b is the measured peak (at MeasuredBlockSize) plus 2 (b - MeasuredBlockSize) x this x H1 / 1e6. Measured by the decision-62 step-1 acceptance (PBS 46685, two-edge p4, H1 7,973,827): Palace peak 45.6 GB at b = 6 (12 resident fields) vs 91.1 GB at b = 48 (96 fields) -> 0.542 GB per field = 0.068 GB per million H1 DOFs (node peak used 90.8 -> 136.5 GiB sampled) KEPT by the library-qualification.json refit as an upper bound: the streaming one-pass Gram executable keeps N x (4 Q_local + L_local) x 8 bytes resident whatever b, so any b > 48 adds at most this much (not re-measured: every reducer ran at b = 48)

ReducerPeakStreaming.Rule: ReducerPalacePeakGBEstimate of every reducer stage under the streaming one-pass Gram executable (decision 62(4)): SafetyFactor x PalaceGBPerGiB x (NodeBaselineGiB + (NodeUsedGiBPerMillionH1 + NodeUsedGiBPerMillionH1PerSource x sources) x H1 / 1e6) - a conservative NODE-USED figure (>= SafetyFactor x every measured node-used peak below), not Palace's own peak: the streaming reducer evaluates every source once and keeps N x (4 Q_local + L_local) x 8 bytes resident, so its peak no longer grows with PALACE_RESPONSE_BLOCK_SIZE (the Previous term's resident-field growth, 84 x 0.068 GB per million H1 at b = 48, was 2-3x the measured streaming peaks and sent the p5-control jobs of the largest thin coupons to the r8g fallback; USER decision 2026-09-22 (B): re-measured on library-device-thin-01's p3 / p4 / p5 reducers, the previous term kept as ReducerPalacePeakGBEstimatePrevious). Estimate / measured node-used ratios on the measured rows: 1.53-2.05 (the line itself holds every row without the factor; the coefficients are the tightest round values doing so: measured p5 controls 1.9-2.2 GiB per million H1 above a ~40 GiB baseline, the p4 main reducers 3.7-4.6 with 120-175 sources - the per-source term; the p3 controls are baseline-dominated). At these coefficients every device coupon of decision 64a (fabricated and thin) plans on m8g.48xlarge: the largest job estimate is the fabricated 3-edge-5d3b p4 reducer, 447 GiB of the 460.8 GiB threshold

Previous.Rule: measured per-stage ReducerPalacePeakGB (b28f089a... executable at block size 6, four-edge-physics-11) x the H1 ratio + 2 (b - 6) x ReducerResidentFieldGBPerMillionH1 x H1 / 1e6 resident fields (decision 62(1) calibration, PBS 46685)

ReducerPeakStreaming.CarriedRule: carried by the library-qualification.json refit unchanged: the block is a node-used calibration of the streaming executable (USER decision 2026-09-22 (B), library-device-thin-01's reducers), not re-derivable from the Palace peaks this refit reads; its Executable is checked against the run's frozen executable; estimate_stages applies it to every reducer stage of this model

RateRule: per stage and quantity the largest value over the run's coupons after scaling to the reference H1 (the per-source non-solve seconds from the largest worker-block mean per-source seconds of the coupon, so every block of a split coupon is covered; the worker's non-source seconds per worker job) (times, peaks: x H1_ref / H1_c; node used GiB: the largest non-Palace remainder plus the reference peak; the reducer block-pair seconds: divided by the estimator's evaluation / Gram scale of the coupon relative to the reference source count; per-source archive GB: x H1 ratio / sources); the worker's non-source and the reducer's setup seconds are wall-based (wall - sources x mean per-source seconds / wall - block-pair seconds) so launch overhead is inside the estimate; MeanPerSourceSeconds = the largest per-source non-solve seconds + the largest seconds per PCG iteration x the largest mean PCG count

Previous.Provenance: the model every qualify run up to this refit used: Measured per-stage cost rates of the Palace response worker / reducer / ordinary local-edge stages on one r8g.48xlarge node (192 ranks, frozen b28 executable), from the four-edge-physics-11 V-a run (PBS 45145; results/main/cost-summary.json and status.json of coupon-accuracy-assessment-20260913/four-edge-physics-11). estimate_stages.py scales them to another hybrid prism-tube coupon mesh by the exact H1 DOF ratio (time per PCG iteration, reducer, memory) with 1x / 1.5x / 2x the measured mean PCG counts; the same method predicted the physics-11 V-a run from physics-09 GO within 2% (47 vs 48 min, 187 vs 187 GB) and the gallery-06b run from V-a.

SelfCheck.Rule: estimate_stages on every coupon of the run under this model, read per job as the split planner does: at the measured PCG counts every stage's estimate over its measured wall is >= 1 (MinimumStageEstimateOverActual) and so is every job's; the jobs at the worst PCG factor with preflight and margin over the coupon's measured node seconds is the conservatism ratio (EstimateWorstWithMarginOverActual); FitsOneJob is the single-job decision under this model; PreviousModel is the same check under the previous model
